correctness.rationale: On the predator-free orbit the prey rises logistically from kappa*h_l/eta to h_l/eta, where kappa=1-p_1 E_l is in (0,1). Integrating the logistic reciprocal velocity gives the stated T>0 when 0<h_l<eta K; equality with eta K gives infinite time. At the event, d[eta*x+(1-eta)*y]/dt=eta*r*x*(1-x/K)>0, so the local return time is smooth under the source regularity assumptions. Parameterize the postharvest section by y; one-dimensional return is y times (1-p_2 E_l) times the exponential of the integrated per-capita predator rate. At y=0 that rate is -mu since psi(0)=0; variation of the event time affects no linear predator term because y vanishes on the orbit. The return derivative is (1-p_2 E_l) exp(-mu*T) in (0,1), also at p_2=0, proving local orbital asymptotic stability. The printed convergence ratio reduces to the same expression by integrating d(log x)/dt=r-rx/K. The independent replay /workspace/replay_2.py integrates in prey position and checks exactly exp(r*T)=4, the threshold 3/16 and rho=2/5 at p_2=1/10 (rho=3/10 for the original baseline p_2=1/5). This is a modified baseline example, not Xu–Zou's separate subthreshold run, which hits the infinite-time boundary. Theorem 2.2(1)'s reliance on boundary instability is not a proof of nonexistence of any positive cycle.

value.rationale: Scientifically, the exact multiplier corrects a qualitative stability reversal for a natural extinction cycle and names the false premise of an argument about positive cycles. It has a concrete example away from the degenerate hitting boundary. The mathematical correction is useful, but publishing this frozen result again would duplicate the earlier correction.
